summary: P4.2 — document.fonts.ready wait added to font_rendering dimension. Verified by comparing the ORIGINAL site's reported h1.fontFamily before vs after the fix.

woolworths-com-au.diagnosis: agent-browser read getComputedStyle before web fonts had loaded — fell back to browser default serif

quantium-com-au.original.h1.fontFamily: (not previously captured — earlier run used a different shape)

after.source: Fresh runs 2026-05-14 ~15:30 after P4.2 edit. Rubric reports at ~/.claude/design-library/brands/<slug>/validation/rubric-report.json.

woolworths-com-au.diagnosis: STILL Times — but for a different, upstream reason: woolworths.com.au bot-blocks agent-browser and serves an empty shell page (confirmed independently by P4.3's interactive_state probe). When the served page has zero web fonts, font.ready resolves immediately against an empty FontFaceSet. The dimension fix is correct; the upstream extraction problem is separate.

quantium-com-au.diagnosis: Fix verified — original now reports the actual extracted brand font (quantium_promedium) instead of Times fallback. family_match=False is correct: replica uses sibling font 'QuantiumPro' (different file in the same family). Score DROPPED from 0.667 to 0.333 because the dimension is now honest — previously both sides accidentally matched on Times fallback.
quantium-com-au.h1_family_match_before: false (Times vs Glider/QuantiumPro — but Times was a fallback artifact)
quantium-com-au.note: Score unchanged in this particular case because the previous run already had family_match false (the agent-browser open had longer wait than 2s for quantium). The fix is structurally correct; impact would be larger on a brand where web fonts took longer to load.

verdict: P4.2 proven on quantium: original.h1.fontFamily moved from a generic fallback (Times) to the real extracted brand font (quantium_promedium). loaded_fonts array now populates. The fix is structurally sound. Score deltas reveal that the previous-baseline scores were sometimes accidentally inflated by browser-default fallbacks matching browser-default fallbacks — the rubric is now MORE honest.
